checks.reason: Datadog API auth page: write requests require an API key and read requests also require an application key; no OAuth described for general API use.
Pricing page offers a permanent Free tier ('up to five Basic hosts with 1-day metric retention, at no cost') and says trials can move to the Free tier, so credentials are obtainable at $0.
Datadog's API reference is an HTTP/JSON REST API authenticated with API/application keys.
Datadog's own docs describe the 'Remote Datadog MCP Server' that provides remote access to most Datadog products (noted as under significant development, not GovCloud).
Free tier plus self-serve API/app keys means a toolkit can be built and tested today without gates.
Atlassian docs describe OAuth 2.0 (3LO) apps created self-serve in the developer console; basic auth/API tokens are only for simple scripts and collecting customer tokens is discouraged.
Jira pricing lists a Free plan, and 3LO apps can be created and shared without mandatory review (unreviewed apps only show a warning).
Jira Cloud platform is accessed via REST APIs (page refers to making REST API calls with 3LO or basic auth).
Atlassian developer docs describe its cloud-hosted Rovo MCP server at https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp.
Free site plus self-serve OAuth 3LO app creation allows building and testing today; review only affects the 'unreviewed app' warning.
Asana auth docs say OAuth is 'the best choice if multiple users need to sign in to your app'; PATs are for scripts, service accounts are Enterprise-only.
Asana developer overview says you can 'create a free account' to build/test (sandbox only needed for premium features).
Quick start uses REST endpoints such as https://app.asana.com/api/1.0/workspaces with a PAT.
Asana's developer docs state 'Asana offers a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server' hosted at https://mcp.asana.com/v2/mcp.
Free account plus self-serve OAuth/PAT credentials; no review gate stated for building and testing.
Coda (now Superhuman Docs) API reference uses 'Authorization: Bearer <your API token>' user API tokens; no OAuth for third-party API apps is described.
API page: 'We make the Superhuman Docs API available to all of our users free of charge, in both free and paid workspaces.'
Coda API v1 is a REST/JSON API (GET/POST/PUT/PATCH endpoints with rate limits per method).

Coda's own guide says 'Superhuman Docs runs an MCP server built on the open Model Context Protocol standard' (endpoint coda.io/apis/mcp per its help center); community servers also exist but the vendor one is first-party.

The API is free for all users in free and paid workspaces with self-serve tokens, and no review, paid tier, per-tenant setup or enterprise gate is documented, so it meets 'ready' (rate limits and token-only auth are not gates).
Stripe docs: 'Stripe uses API keys to authenticate requests' (secret/restricted/agent keys); OAuth exists for Connect/Apps/MCP but API keys are the core API auth.
Any account gets sandbox test keys (sk_test_/rk_test_) for free to build and test; live keys come with account activation.
Stripe API is a REST API (v1 and v2 endpoints) authenticated by API keys.
Stripe docs document its own hosted MCP server at https://mcp.stripe.com with OAuth or agent API keys.
Free sandbox keys allow a toolkit to be built and tested today.
SIGNED endpoints need an API key plus a request signature; 'We support HMAC, RSA, and Ed25519 keys' (Ed25519 recommended, still a signature scheme).
Spot Test Network gives API keys free via 'Log In with GitHub' with virtual funds; live keys need 2FA, KYC and a deposit of any amount (FAQ 360002502072) but no approval.
Binance Spot API docs are organized as REST API (with WebSocket API/streams alongside); primary style REST matches.
Binance Developer Docs document 'a Binance AI Tool' MCP server at https://agent.binance.com/mcp/agentic (Agent OS); the many GitHub Binance MCPs are community.
Buildable on testnet today, but live keys require KYC, 2FA and a deposit (and regional restrictions), which limits launch.
Xero API access is OAuth2 (custom connections with client ID/secret or OAuth bearer tokens), as documented in Xero's own repo.
Xero developer pricing has a Starter tier at $0 with 5 connections and no certification required; higher tiers are paid and Plus+ need App Certification.
Xero's Accounting API and related APIs are REST/JSON APIs wrapped by the MCP server.
The MCP server is published in Xero's XeroAPI GitHub org as @xeroapi/xero-mcp-server (local npx server).
Testable free on Starter (5 connections) but scaling needs paid tiers and App Certification/security assessment.
Fathom supports API keys for personal use and OAuth apps for integrations other users install; OAuth app registration is a self-serve form (fathom.video/marketplace_applications/new).
Fathom API page: 'API keys, webhooks, and SDKs are included on every Fathom plan, including Free.'
API overview: 'All REST API resources are authenticated with API keys generated via the Fathom website's settings area.'
Fathom's developer docs describe an 'official MCP (Model Context Protocol) server' at https://api.fathom.ai/mcp.
Free plan includes API keys and OAuth apps are self-registered; review only applies to promotion.
Quickstart uses 'Authorization: Bearer $REDUCTO_API_KEY' with keys created in Studio.
Pricing: Standard plan includes '$150 in free usage' (no time limit stated) and quickstart says sign up for a free account and create a key.
Quickstart shows cURL REST calls (plus SDKs wrapping the REST API).
Reducto docs document a hosted MCP server at https://mcp.reducto.ai/mcp and local package mcp-server-reducto.
Free account with self-serve API key lets a toolkit be built and tested today.
Devin API uses service-user credentials / PATs (cog_ prefix) sent as Bearer tokens, i.e. API keys.
Pricing comparison table marks 'Devin API' as not included on Free ($0) and included on Pro ($20/mo), Max, Teams and Enterprise.
Devin API reference is a REST API (v3 organization/enterprise endpoints, legacy v1/v2).
Devin docs document the official Devin MCP server at https://mcp.devin.ai/mcp using a Devin API key.
Buildable with self-serve keys but requires at least the paid Pro plan, a paid-tier gate.
